record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: Fix a Diophantine vector α in T^n. Let U_α be the set of smooth zero-average functions φ on T^n such that the exact symplectic map F_φ(θ,r) = (θ + r, r + ∂φ/∂θ(θ + r)) preserves an invariant torus graph on which F_φ is smoothly conjugate to the translation R_α: θ ↦ θ + α. Is the boundary ∂U_α, viewed in the smooth function space C^∞(T^n), locally a C^k submanifold for some finite k ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Is the boundary ∂Uα of Uα in C∞(Tn) a locally flat Ck-submanifold (for some k ≥ 0) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\geq 1$ and let $\mathbb{T}^n=\mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$. Fix a Diophantine vector $\alpha\in\mathbb{T}^n$, i.e. there exist $\gamma>0$ and $\tau>n-1$ such that $|k\cdot\alpha-m|\geq \gamma|k|^{-\tau}$ for every $k\in\mathbb{Z}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and every $m\in\mathbb{Z}$. For each smooth function $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^n)$ with zero average, consider the exact symplectic map of $\mathbb{T}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n$ defined by
$$F_\varphi(\theta,r)=\bigl(\theta+r,\; r+\partial_\theta\varphi(\theta+r)\bigr).$$
Let $U_\alpha\subset C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^n)$ denote the set of all such zero-average $\varphi$ for which $F_\varphi$ admits an invariant graph torus on which $F_\varphi$ is smoothly conjugate to the translation $R_\alpha:\theta\mapsto\theta+\alpha$. Equip $C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^n)$ with its standard Fréchet topology.

Question: Is the boundary $\partial U_\alpha$ of $U_\alpha$ in $C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^n)$ locally a $C^k$-submanifold (in particular, locally flat) for some finite $k\geq 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not return any source explicitly resolving the question of whether the boundary of the KAM set $U_\alpha$ in $C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^n)$ is locally a $C^k$ submanifold. Related work on the break-up of invariant tori and Herman-type conjectures discusses the boundary of KAM regions but does not appear to settle this local manifold regularity question. The status is therefore unverified.

status_evidence.title: Towards an Understanding of the Break-up of Invariant Tori
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of breakup boundaries for KAM invariant tori without resolving local submanifold regularity of the boundary in C^infty.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on KAM boundary breakup does not establish the local C^k-submanifold structure of the KAM set boundary.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to KAM theory with a view to celestial mechanics (Féjoz)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing Diophantine quasi-periodic tori and Herman-type open questions about accumulation/structure of KAM sets.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of KAM theory list structural questions about the KAM set as open without addressing this precise boundary regularity claim.
